newsitem.title: IRAQ: Iraq says U.S. strike kills five, wounds 19.
newsitem.headline: Iraq says U.S. strike kills five, wounds 19.

text.p: Baghdad said on Tuesday five people were killled and 19 wounded -- including civilians -- in a U.S. cruise missile strike on its air defence positions in south Iraq, an army spokesman said.

"Our sacrifices were five martyrs and 19 wounded among them a group of civilians. A number of residential houses for the citizens were destroyed," the spokesman for Iraq's general command of the armed forces, quoted by state television, said.
He added that U.S. missiles hit civilian areas in "the outskirts of our steadfast cities" as well as military sites but did not name the attacked areas.
The spokesman said the attack would "increase the determination of the mujahideen (holy fighters) to snatch their rights".
He said the result of the attack would disappoint the U.S. and those siding with it in its "aggression against Iraq".
President Saddam Hussein urged his armed forces to resist U.S. strikes and hit back at U.S., British and French warplanes policing no-fly zones in his country.
U.S. military sources said 27 long-range cruise missiles were fired against air defence and communications targets in southern Iraq on Tuesday in retaliation for Iraqi military attacks against Kurds.
